input.quote: 5.8.1 Harpoon shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to (a) directly or indirectly, develop, commercialize or otherwise exploit any Competing Product in any country or other jurisdiction in the Territory, or (b) license, authorize, appoint, or otherwise enable any Third Party to directly or indirectly, develop, commercialize or otherwise exploit any Competing Product in any country or other jurisdiction in the Territory, except, in each case ((a) and (b)), as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement.
input.rationale: The only exclusivity/non-compete architecture in the Agreement runs in our favour. Section 5.8 (Exclusivity with Respect to the Territory) binds Harpoon and its Affiliates not to develop, commercialize or license Competing Products in the Territory, with the Section 5.8.2 carve-outs (Acquisition/Change in Control with Segregation) also giving AbbVie unilateral information-flow and JGC termination rights. Similarly, the Section 5.1.3 grants to AbbVie are exclusive (including as against Harpoon and its Affiliates), and Section 5.9.1 restricts only Harpoon's third-party in-licensing. Searches for supply/sourcing restrictions found no obligation on AbbVie to purchase exclusively or refrain from third-party sourcing: Section 4.5.1 gives AbbVie the sole right (not obligation) to Manufacture or have Manufactured and supply Licensed Compounds and Products, and the Section 10.4 AbbVie covenants are limited to obtaining IP rights from its personnel. This meets the preferred position — no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on the Customer — so no redline is warranted; the Harpoon-side exclusivity is a benefit to us and should be preserved.
